anomaly: Anomalos: not level. The one red dot among blue ones.
Anomaly in the data: a spike on the chart that doesn’t fit the trend.
antipathy: Anti + pathos: a feeling against. A natural antipathy toward liars.
Antipathy = the reverse of sympathy: you can’t stand each other.
appease: Apaiser: bring peace by giving in. Munich 1938: appeasing Hitler.
Appease the toddler with a biscuit: calm him by conceding.
arduous: Arduus = steep. An arduous trek up a mountain.
Arduous: ardu: a task that is hard going.
askance: Look askance = glance sideways in doubt. « De travers ».
Askance: your eyebrow rises as you peek at the strange menu.
banality: Banal + ity: the quality of being ordinary. The banality of small talk.
Banality: the clichés of a coffee-machine chat.
bolster: A bolster pillow props up your head. Bolster = prop up. Evidence bolsters the case.
Bolster morale: the coach’s pep talk strengthens the team.
capricious: Capra = goat: leaps without warning. A capricious monarch changes his mind daily.
Capricious weather: sun, then storm, then sun.
contrition: Con + terere (crush): a heart worn down by guilt. A contrite apology.
Contrition: sobbing at confession. Genuine remorse.
craven: Craven = defeated, gives up. A craven coward who runs.
Craven sounds like “crave in”: crying for mercy at the first threat.
deleterious: Greek deleterios: harmful. Smoking has deleterious effects on health.
Délétère: gas leaking in a lab. Harmful.
dilatory: Dilatare: to delay. A dilatory student postpones the essay all week.
Dilatory tactics: stalling in the meeting.
dispassionate: Dis + passion: no passion. A dispassionate judge analyses the facts.
Dispassionate: a scientist reading numbers, calm.
disseminate: Dis + seminare (sow): sow seeds widely. Disseminate information through the press.
Disseminate: spread the news like pollen.
duress: Durus = hard: pressure. A signature under duress is not valid.
Duress: confessing with a knife at your back.
economical: Oikonomia: house management. An economical car uses little fuel; economical prose wastes no word.
Economical with the truth: says as little truth as possible. A polite way to say he lies.
edifying: Aedificare: build up. An edifying lecture builds your mind.
Edifying: a documentary that improves you morally or mentally.
efficacious: Efficacious sounds like effective: it does the job.
elicit: E + lacere (lure): lure out. Elicit a smile.
Elicit information from a reluctant witness: draw it out gently.
erudite: E + rudis (rough): polished from rough. A professor so erudite that he quotes Latin.
Erudite: someone who has read the whole library.
esoteric: Esoterikos: inner. Esoteric rituals understood only by insiders.
Esoteric knowledge: a secret society’s handbook.
fastidious: Fastidium: disgust. Fussy about every detail: not “fastidieux”.
A fastidious chef rejects a tomato for one blemish.
flux: Fluere: flow. Everything is in flux; the situation changes constantly.
Flux: a river never the same twice.
furtive: Fur = thief. A furtive glance, stolen quickly.
Furtive: slipping out of the room unseen.
harried: Harry: raid. Harried by deadlines like an army attacking.
A harried mother of three: always rushed.
ignominious: In + nomen (name): losing your good name. An ignominious defeat.
Ignominious: a king dethroned and paraded in shame.
impartial: Im + partial: not taking a side. An impartial referee.
imprudent: In + prudens: lacking foresight. An imprudent investor puts everything on one bet.
indecorous: In + decorous: improper. Indecorous laughter at a funeral.
Indecorous behaviour: breaking the rules of polite society.
jovial: Jove (Jupiter): cheerful. A jovial host with a loud laugh.
maladroit: Mal + adroit: bad right hand. A maladroit remark that offends.
Maladroit: he spills the wine on the host.
maverick: Samuel Maverick refused to brand his calves: an independent. Top Gun’s call sign.
A maverick scientist ignoring the consensus.
misconstrue: Mis + construe: build the wrong meaning. She misconstrued his joke as an insult.
Misconstrue: reading the wrong message into a text.
mundane: Mundus = world: everyday earthly things. Mundane tasks: laundry, emails.
Mundane: the commute: tedious and ordinary.
nonplussed: Non plus: no more to say. Totally baffled.
Nonplussed: you stare, speechless, at a surprising question.
nuance: Nue = cloud: shades. A nuance of meaning: subtle.
Nuance: the difference between grey and gris perle.
opulence: Ops = wealth: lavish luxury. The opulence of Versailles.
pejorative: Pejor = worse. A pejorative term makes it sound bad.
Pejorative: calling a country “backward”: an insulting label.
placate: Placare: to calm. Placate the customer with a refund.
Placate: give the baby a pacifier.
polemic: Polemos = war: a war of words. A polemic against the government.
Polemic: a newspaper column that attacks.
posit: Ponere: to put. Posit a theory: put it forward.
Posit: “let’s assume X”: you set it down as a starting point.
rebuke: Re + buke: beat back. The teacher’s rebuke silenced the class.
reproach: Re + prope: bring back to the near: you throw the fault back. Beyond reproach = spotless.
Reproach: the sad look from a disappointed parent.
specious: Species: appearance. A specious argument looks good but is wrong.
Specious = “spacious”: seems big but is hollow.
stringent: Stringere: tighten. Stringent rules: tight and strict.
sullen: Solus: alone. A sullen teenager in a corner.
Sullen: grumpy silence at the table.
timorous: Timor: fear. A timorous kitten under the sofa.
Timorous voice trembling when asked to speak.
transient: Trans + ire: passing through. Transient guests stay one night.
Transient: a cloud passing, gone soon.
truncate: Truncus: trunk. Cut it short: a truncated report loses its ending.
Truncate: chop the end off, like a trimmed tree.
